about.title: Walnut Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Walnut is a quieter city than many of its Los Angeles County neighbors, but that doesn't mean falls don't happen — in shopping centers along Grand Avenue, apartment walkways near Amar Road, or restaurants off Lemon Avenue and La Puente Road. A slip, trip, or fall on someone else's property can happen in seconds: a wet floor with no sign, a cracked walkway, poor lighting in a stairwell, or an unmarked spill. What matters afterward is whether the property owner or manager knew, or should have known, about the hazard and did nothing to fix or warn about it. That's the heart of a California premises liability claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured Walnut residents and visitors with an independent attorney who can review what happened, look at surveillance footage before it's erased, and explain your options. The consultation is free, and there's no fee unless the attorney recovers something for you.

Shoulder dislocations and rotator cuff tears

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Walnut Fall

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to act. An attorney can help gather the evidence needed to establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Walnut businesses and complexes overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, a Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for a fall, you may still recover a share of damages. An attorney can help sort out how fault gets divided in your specific situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Walnut?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a claim against a private property owner. If the property involved is government-owned, the deadline is much shorter and involves an early claim filing requirement. Because these timelines are strict, it's worth speaking with an attorney as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my own fall?
items.answer: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still pursue compensation even if you share some blame for the fall. Your potential recovery would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't eliminated. An attorney can help evaluate how the facts of your situation might be viewed.

items.question: Does it matter that Walnut doesn't have heavy traffic or high crash numbers?
items.answer: Not really — premises liability claims are separate from roadway collisions. Walnut's crash data shows relatively low injury collision counts along corridors like Amar Road and La Puente Road, but slip and fall cases happen inside stores, complexes, and parking lots regardless of nearby traffic patterns. What matters is the condition of the property where you fell, not the surrounding road statistics.
